wa_secondary_face.blurb: Secondary Face is a small wall at Minnehaha, the granite crag on Spokane's northeast side. It tucks away behind the Main Wall and a neighboring wall, a short trail walk from the parking lot. Ten climbs mix traditional and bolted lines, and the grades run from easy fifth class (5.7) up into the 5.12 range, with the larger share of routes being trad. Cracks and corners at the friendlier end make it a decent spot for gear practice, while a few harder bolted and gear lines give stronger climbers something to work on. It works well as a side stop from the busier main faces.

wa_semantics.blurb: Semantics is a bouldering zone in the Skykomish Valley, in the western Cascades about an hour from Seattle, sitting on high ground around 3,600 feet. It is part of the Treasury, 2nd Field cluster of boulders. Ten problems range from V3 up to V8, with the middle of the range around V4 to V6, so it suits people who already climb solidly. The namesake boulder is a big, shaded block with an undercut roof, and its lines vary in style from squeezing and pressing to powerful moves and tense top-outs. To get there, drop down from the Whiteface boulder and head upstream along the trail into the denser trees.

wa_south_wall.blurb: South Wall is the southern end of the Lower Crag in the Chewiliken Creek crags of the Okanogan, near Tonasket. It offers short face climbs of good quality gathered around a large corner, with a shorter upper wall nearby that faces south. Ten routes, nearly all of them traditional with one bolted line, run from about 5.6 to 5.10, and most sit in the 5.6 to 5.9 range, which makes it friendly for climbers building up on gear. The rock toward this end of the valley is described as better than what lies farther north. The usual way in is a 20-minute-plus hike up the creek from the southwest.

wa_stone_s_throw.blurb: Stone's Throw is a roadside formation in the Eight Mile Area of Icicle Creek, a few miles up the canyon from Leavenworth at roughly 1,900 feet. It holds ten routes split evenly between sport and trad, with grades from about 5.8 to 5.10, so it fits climbers working through the lower double digits or just starting on gear. Some routes can also be top-roped. Cracks, including a slot on the left half of the formation, take gear, and several lines are reported to be accumulating moss. Plan on short, single-pitch outings rather than a full day of mileage.

wa_the_goods.blurb: The Goods sits at the eastern, rear end of Stegosaurus Butte, in the Middle Fork valley near North Bend. It is part of The Rump, a cluster known for continuous crack systems. Ten routes here are nearly all traditional, with a single bolted line, running from about 5.8 up to the low 5.12 range and concentrated around 5.10 and 5.11. Expect a mix of single-pitch and multi-pitch lines on the butte. The walk in is long and steep through mossy forested talus, passing other walls on the way, so it is a poor choice for small children or dogs.

wa_upper_clamshell_cave.blurb: Upper Clamshell Cave is a tier of short climbs perched just above the main Clamshell Cave wall in Icicle Canyon, near Leavenworth, at about 2,000 feet. Ten routes cover mostly bolted sport lines, a couple of top-ropes and a pair of trad lines, with grades from around 5.6 up to 5.11. Moderates sit toward the far end, while a roof and some steep bolted lines mark the other side. Reach it by following the trail that skirts the left side of the lower wall, then turn right once you arrive at the bolted roof.
